name: Ram Silence
description: Ram Silence is a small, airless barren world whose name derives from the absolute absence of sound on its surface and the ram-like profile of its largest mountain formation, a double-peaked ridge that dominates the northern hemisphere. The exposed planetary core is visible in the walls of a massive equatorial canyon, its metallic gleam the only bright feature in a landscape of dark, impact-scarred regolith. Solar wind has polished the windward surfaces to a dull sheen while leaving the leeward faces rough and cratered.

The silence on Ram Silence is not merely quiet but total, a vacuum of sound that makes the visual landscape feel like a photograph rather than a place. The shadows are absolute black, the sunlit surfaces blinding white, and there is no gradient between them. The low gravity allows dust displaced by footfalls to arc in perfect parabolas, each grain following its ballistic trajectory with mechanical precision before settling minutes later in a location it may occupy for millennia.

A distress beacon orbits Ram Silence, transmitting on standard emergency frequencies with no identifying information. The beacon has been operating for an estimated fifteen years, its power source consistent with a standard escape pod transmitter, but no pod or wreckage has been located on the surface or in orbit. The beacon's signal shows no sign of degradation, suggesting either exceptional engineering or periodic maintenance by an unknown party. Search-and-rescue protocols require investigation of all active distress beacons, but multiple sweeps have found nothing.

Ram Silence has no commercial value and no strategic significance beyond the unresolved mystery of the distress beacon. The titanium deposits in the exposed core are modest and more easily obtained elsewhere. The beacon continues to transmit its call for help into the void, unanswered and unexplained, a small electronic voice repeating in the silence of a world that has nothing else to say. Pilots in the sector have learned to log the signal and move on, but the question of who is calling and why has never been resolved.
